functional_semantics.triton: C = A @ B, fp32 accumulator, cast to c dtype at the store (impl_triton.py:67-79).
functional_semantics.cutile: C = A @ B, fp32 accumulator, cast to C.dtype at the store (impl_cutile.py:55-68).
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py:21-27 (torch.matmul under allow_tf32=True; fp8 via _scaled_mm with unit scales then cast to e4m3fn). Generator tensors.py:416-436 scales both operands by K**-0.5 and returns row-major (a, b).

stages.triton: allocation + descriptor construction + one GEMM launch (impl_triton.py:131-164).
stages.note: Single-kernel blocked GEMM with grouped tile ordering on both sides (impl_triton.py:54-62, impl_cutile.py:43-53).

dependencies.triton: kernel depends on c and on bt (impl_triton.py:132,137-139).
dependencies.note: No intermediates besides the Triton-side bt (see preprocessing).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: sequential K loop in BLOCK_K chunks via tl.range, MMA accumulation (impl_triton.py:69-76).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: sequential K loop with compile-time trip count, MMA accumulation (impl_cutile.py:56-66).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same ascending-k sequential reduction; no split-K on either side.

precision.triton: input_precision='tf32' passed for every dtype (impl_triton.py:76): TF32 operands for fp32, native fp16/fp8 operands otherwise; fp32 accumulation; single cast at the store (79).
precision.cutile: mma_dtype = tfloat32 only when A is fp32, else native dtype (impl_cutile.py:59,63,65); fp32 accumulation; single cast at the store (68).
precision.note: Effectively the same precision path on both sides (the tf32 flag is a no-op for non-fp32 operands). fp8 is consumed unscaled on both sides, consistent with the reference's unit scales. Both round the fp32 accumulator once to e4m3fn whereas the reference rounds via bf16 (impl_torch.py:24-26); config.verify atol 5.0 / rtol 0.1 covers it.

preprocessing.triton: bt = b.t().contiguous() (N, K) cached in the module-level plain dict _bt_cache keyed by (b.data_ptr(), shape, dtype), never evicted (impl_triton.py:32-39), looked up on every run (132): the transpose copy executes once per distinct B (warmup) and is untimed thereafter.
preprocessing.cutile: B consumed row-major as (TK, TN) tiles directly (impl_cutile.py:64-65); no cache, no transpose, no descriptors.
preprocessing.note: Genuine F/Q boundary divergence: one side's steady-state timed region is 'GEMM with a prepacked K-major B', the other's is 'GEMM over the delivered layout'. The reference applies a similar cached repack only for fp8 (impl_torch.py:10-18). Not resolvable by intersection; the contract requires any repack to be per call and uncached and lists the question as open.

intermediate_storage.triton: bt (N, K) retained for the process lifetime per (data_ptr, shape, dtype) key (impl_triton.py:32-39); unbounded growth across the 60-case sweep.
intermediate_storage.note: Cross-call persistent operand copy vs none; same root cause as the preprocessing divergence. The address-keyed plain dict is also a stale-address hazard (a freed B's address reused by a same-shape, same-dtype B would receive stale data).

mutation.triton: a, b never written; fresh c per call (impl_triton.py:131).
mutation.cutile: a, b never written; fresh c per call (impl_cutile.py:82).
mutation.note: Idempotent for a fixed B object; see the stale-address hazard above.

hardware_dispatch.triton: no dispatch branches (host TMA descriptor path only, impl_triton.py:137-139,150-152).
hardware_dispatch.cutile: no dispatch branches; per-dtype default configs (impl_cutile.py:13-17).
hardware_dispatch.note: Descriptor-based vs tile loads and compile-time K (impl_cutile.py:39) are mapping details.

fq_boundary.bytes_expr: (M * K + K * N + M * N) * dtype_size
fq_boundary.note: The formula counts A once, B once and C once in the input dtype. The cuTile path matches it with B consumed in its delivered (K, N) layout and no cache. The Triton path matches it in steady state only because the K-major copy of B (read + write of K*N elements plus one copy launch) is executed once per distinct B address and cached in _bt_cache (impl_triton.py:32-39,132), i.e. never timed after warmup: the formula implicitly credits a free prepacked B on that side. A generated implementation that transposes B per call carries 2*K*N*dtype_size of uncounted timed traffic; one reading B natively matches the formula. The reference's fp8 path (impl_torch.py:10-18) caches an analogous repack by data_ptr; its fp32/fp16 paths do not.

review_items: Decide whether the K-major repack of B is inside the timed algorithm: the contract requires any repack to be per call and uncached, but the manual Triton timing excludes it (bt cached in _bt_cache, impl_triton.py:32-39,132); either re-measure the Triton reference with a per-call transpose or direct (K, N) consumption, or mark its numbers as not comparable to contract-conforming implementations.

Fix or flag the manual Triton _bt_cache (impl_triton.py:32-39): a plain dict keyed by (data_ptr, shape, dtype) that is never evicted is a stale-address correctness hazard when a freed B's address is reused and retains every (N, K) copy across the 60-case sweep; matmul_int8 already uses a WeakTensorKeyDictionary for the same purpose.

Confirm the fp32 reference precision at verification time: impl_torch.py:4 sets torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True at import and never restores it, while matmul_int8's reference sets it to False inside run() without restoring; the contract permits TF32 operand rounding on the assumption that the reference is also TF32-class under the atol 5.0 / rtol 0.1 tolerance.
